approach: Add `check_reader_question(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>` in the new `crates/athena-core/src/reading/questions.rs`. Declare it in `reading.rs` and run it as the first `step!` of `refusing_check` in `reading/checks.rs`. Every reading-text rule runs there, and `read_for` reaches it through `check_reading_acceptance` straight after `build_reading` (reading.rs:659-689), as do `check_reading_text` (replay, `athena check-reading`, steward) and the refusal corpus. A reading with no question passes. A question is accepted only when it begins `User:` (same normalisation as `admission::has_addressee`; `Host:` is refused). It must not say the code answers it (reuse `says_code_answers`). It must hold at least two distinct non-empty alternatives labelled `(a)`/`(b)` or `(1)`/`(2)`, where a label counts only at the start of the text or after whitespace or `:`, so `file(s)` is not a label. It must end with `Default: (x)`, where `(x)` is one of those labels. A refusal lists every gap, quotes the question and gives the repair: settle it from the repository or defaults and leave `question` null, or write `User:` + the decision + labelled alternatives + `Default: (a)`. To stop every first question being refused, the form is also taught up front. A 12th line in `READING_RULES` (crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs), modelled on the planner's `OPEN_QUESTION_RULE`, names `check_reader_question` and the form. It is pinned by the existing reading-rules test in briefs.rs. The line sits in the reader brief, which is outside the reader token budget (lib.rs:284-285 composes `CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults, catalog` only), so no prompt file or budget line changes. `admission.rs` only widens `has_addressee` and `says_code_answers` to `pub(crate)` and adds a `pub(crate)` `is_user_addressed` helper that shares one normalisation. Planner open-questions behaviour is unchanged. The change also needs unit tests, 17 corpus cases, updates to the reading tests that reach the gate with a question, a CHANGELOG entry and a design-doc paragraph.

decisions.choice: Run the rule as the first `step!` in `refusing_check` (checks.rs:518-548), not as a bail inside `build_reading`.
decisions.reason: All reading-text rules live there. `no_check_bypasses_refusing_check` and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` (refusal_corpus.rs) enforce it. `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54, used by steward.rs:421 and `athena check-reading`) goes only through `refusing_check`, so a check inside `build_reading` would be invisible to the replay that holds over-refusing jobs. The production path is identical: `read_for` runs `build_reading` then `check_reading_acceptance` back to back. First in the list, so a malformed question costs no extra reader round for a second defect. Answer to finding 5 for the verifier: criterion 1's Grep finds the definition in reading/questions.rs and the call site at the first `step!` of `refusing_check` in reading/checks.rs. `read_for` reaches that call straight after `build_reading`, so the criterion's 'wired after build_reading' holds.

rejected.option: Call the rule from inside `build_reading` (the literal wording of criterion 1).
rejected.why: It skips `check_reading_text`, the replay and the corpus mechanism, and the corpus test would flag a check outside `refusing_check`.
A reading with a bad question and another defect would be refused for the other defect first, costing an extra reader round.

decisions.choice: Teach the form up front with a 12th `READING_RULES` line in crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs, and keep the refusal text as the backstop. Remove the previous open question. Answers finding 2.
decisions.reason: The code settles it. `BudgetSet::Reader` is computed from `CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults, catalog` (crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:284-285), so the reader brief and its rule list sit outside the 71-token headroom. The planner-side rule is likewise both enforced (`open_questions_findings`) and stated in the planner brief (`OPEN_QUESTION_RULE`, briefs/planner.rs:64-66, pinned at briefs.rs:1620-1630). With the line in the brief, the reader writes a valid question the first time. The refusal text only catches a slip, and the customer is not asked about a code fact. `READING_RULES` is the list that names each reading check, and a line there is how earlier rules were taught (CHANGELOG.md lines 113, 138, 169). The brief is not a prompt file; `READER_FRAME` and the other prompt assets stay untouched. Proposed line (under 220 characters, as the existing test requires): 'Reader question: settle it from the repository or defaults; else `question` is `User:` + the decision + alternatives `(a)`, `(b)` + `Default: (a)` (`check_reader_question`).'

rejected.why: Each asking job would cost an extra reader call, and a second malformed question would leave the job with no reading. The brief line costs about 170 bytes of a brief that is outside every token budget.

decisions.choice: Require `User:` only; `Host:` is refused for the reader's question. Share the prefix normalisation through a `pub(crate)` helper in admission.rs.
decisions.reason: Criterion 1 says a question without `User:` is refused. The reader's question is shown to the customer (crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs:392) and answered with `athena correct`, so a host fact is not his decision. One normalisation (leading whitespace, `*`, `_`, backticks, case; `Username:` does not match) cannot drift from the planner's.

rejected.option: Accept `User:` or `Host:` as the planner does.
rejected.why: Contradicts criterion 1; a host fact is for the repository or defaults.

rejected.option: Copy the prefix code into questions.rs.
rejected.why: Two definitions can drift; the brief asks for reuse.

decisions.choice: Detect alternatives by explicit labels `(a)`/`(b)` or `(1)`/`(2)`. A label token is one ASCII letter or 1-2 digits in parentheses, and counts only when preceded by start of text, whitespace or `:`. Need at least 2 distinct labels with non-empty, distinct text, and `Default:` followed by one of those labels. Answers finding 3.
decisions.reason: The check is deterministic and the finding can state the exact form. The preceding-character rule stops `file(s)` and similar from adding a spurious alternative; a corpus case pins `Which file(s)? Default: (s).` as refused, and another pins `file(s)` beside real labels as accepted.

rejected.option: Count the word 'or' or question marks.
rejected.why: 'hello or hi' would pass with no default, and 'ok or not' would count as two alternatives.

rejected.option: Accept any parenthesised token as a label.
rejected.why: `file(s)` becomes a third alternative and `(s)` could be a default.

rejected.option: Accept `a)`, `1.` or prose 'either X or Y' as well.
rejected.why: More forms mean more false accepts and a longer parser; the finding names the single accepted form.

The doc comment, `///` lines collapsed, directly above `pub fn check_reader_question(`, contains 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended', 'expected 3% of newly refused readings', 'estimate', and the cause: questions the repository or defaults could settle cost the customer time. CHANGELOG.md contains `check_reader_question`, 'higher refusal rate is intended' and 'expected 3% of newly refused readings'.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing or reworded doc comment or CHANGELOG entry fails the needle assertions.
demonstrations.seam: Modelled on the existing `history_fixture_refusal_is_declared_intended` in refusal_corpus.rs (exists, ~line 2916). Step 8 adds the new test. It uses `include_str!` of questions.rs and CHANGELOG.md; `replay_declaration` exists in athena-core. No double.

demonstrations.method: A unit test refuses a free-form question through the gate and asserts the text of the error.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. The error from `check_reading_acceptance` for `User: Which file?` names the gaps ('alternatives', 'default'), quotes the question, says to settle the question from the repository or the defaults and leave `question` null, and gives the form `User:` + the decision + alternatives labelled `(a)`, `(b)` + `Default: (a)` with the example `User: Which greeting: (a) hello or (b) hi? Default: (a).`. A second reading with several gaps (no prefix, no alternatives, no default) shows all gaps listed in one error.
demonstrations.fails_without: A refusal that only said 'question refused' lacks the settle-it and required-form phrases the test asserts, so the test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:490) with a `Reading` from the existing `scoped_reading` helper. The error text is produced by `check_reader_question` (step 2). No double.

demonstrations.method: Run fmt and clippy and the updated tests. The reading.rs tests that reach the gate with a question (lines 5787, 5958 including its `{word}` loop, 6048, 6179, 6983, 7942, 8557 in the base snapshot) use a shared valid `User:` question. Tests that call one check directly (4299, 4761, 5023, 7265, 7588, 8155) pass unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: Clippy exits clean. Also run `cargo fmt --all --check` (no diff) and `cargo test -p athena-core reading::` (the updated question tests pass), `cargo test -p athena-context` (the reader-brief rules test, now with 12 rules), and `cargo test --locked` (other crates unaffected).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the test updates, `check_reading_acceptance(&asking, ...).unwrap()` (reading.rs ~5788) and the other gate-reaching question tests fail with the new refusal.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `check_reading_acceptance`/`refusing_check`. One shared `const VALID_QUESTION` in the reading.rs test module, added in step 5 (not step 8, per finding 4). No double.

demonstrations.method: Corpus-file test reads CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/job-planning.md through `include_str!` and asserts the recorded text; a briefs test pins the reader rule line.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. The collapsed CHANGELOG.md contains `check_reader_question`. The collapsed docs/design/job-planning.md contains 'reader_question', 'same addressee rule as the planner', 'open questions', 'alternatives' and 'Default:'. `cargo test -p athena-context the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` shows the 12th rule line names `check_reader_question`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Missing or reworded entries fail the needle assertions; a missing rules line fails the briefs test.
demonstrations.seam: New corpus test (step 8) modelled on existing doc-needle tests in refusal_corpus.rs; briefs test exists and is extended in step 6. No double.
